🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO NEGOTIATES T-MEC FROM STRENGTH — AGENDA CUT FROM 54 ISSUES TO 14

Heading into the next round on July 20, Mexico and the US have narrowed the T-MEC review from 54 contested points down to just 14, with the 4T bloc in the Senate calling the balance 'favorable' for Mexico. The wager: negotiate with strength and dignity because the economy is solid at home — Mexico closed May as the top trading partner of the US, ahead of Canada and China.

🚨🇲🇽 THE CIA IS OPERATING ON MEXICAN SOIL WITHOUT AUTHORIZATION — AND EYEING 2030

A Contralínea investigation maps how US intelligence pressures Mexico's sovereignty: up to 1 million people work for the American spy apparatus worldwide, backed by roughly 800 military bases — 80 to 100 in Latin America and the Caribbean. It took a car crash in Chihuahua last April to expose four undercover CIA agents operating with zero federal authorization. Analyst Nayar López warns that, left unchecked, espionage and influence ops 'could impact the 2030 elections.'

🔥🇲🇽 PEÑA NIETO-ERA PEMEX GRAFT CATCHES UP: EMILIO LOZOYA'S SISTER BOUND FOR TRIAL

A federal judge has ordered Gilda Lozoya — sister of former Pemex chief Emilio Lozoya — to stand trial for money laundering in the Agronitrogenados case: the fertilizer plant Pemex bought under Peña Nieto at a 200-million-dollar overprice. Prosecutors laid out 54 pieces of evidence that she acted as a front to hide the proceeds. Under the 4T, the neoliberal looting finally reaches a courtroom.

🔥🇲🇽 SALINAS PLIEGO'S TV AZTECA FALLS INTO BANKRUPTCY — 228 OF 600 CREDITORS UNPAID

Ricardo Salinas Pliego — the billionaire who bankrolls Mexico's anti-4T opposition — just dragged TV Azteca into concurso mercantil (bankruptcy protection). The filing lists 1,970 debts worth 23.3 billion pesos, up 147% since 2022, with 9.1 billion owed to New York bondholders. Of 600 creditors, 228 haven't been paid in over a month. The oligarch who lectures the country on 'freedom' can't cover his own bills.

LATIN TIMES: Who is 'Carlitos Rugrats,' the alleged Sinaloa Cartel leader targeted by the US?
July 7, 2026 | 🟡

📰 A San Diego indictment charges Carlos Paez Pereda ("Carlitos Rugrats") with narcoterrorism and "material support of terrorism" over fentanyl trafficking — seven counts, life possible. The FBI added him to its Most Wanted list. 🇲🇽

The terrorism counts flow from the foreign-terrorist-organization label the US slapped on Mexican cartels last year, now being tested in a US courtroom.

• DOJ: charged with "narcoterrorism, material support of terrorism and drug trafficking"

EL PAÍS: Mexico will press the US to remove tariffs on autos and steel during the USMCA review
July 9, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Heading into the July 20 USMCA round, Mexico goes on offense: Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard says the 50% US steel-and-aluminum tariff is "unacceptable," with "no justification whatsoever." Autos still pay 25% even under the pact's preferential terms. 🇲🇽

The US declined to renew the "free trade" agreement on July 1, opting for annual reviews instead.

• Ebrard: the 50% rate "has no justification whatsoever"

AP: A Mexican village warned of a cartel offensive during the World Cup. Then the drone attacks began
July 8, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Cartel drones bombed Guajes de Ayala, Guerrero at 6 a.m. — weeks after residents warned authorities. Security analyst David Saucedo says National Guard units were pulled to fortify World Cup host cities, leaving non-host regions exposed. 🇲🇽

The same report notes the counter-cartel vigilantes carried "military-grade weapons smuggled from the U.S." — the arms pipeline that rarely makes the terrorist-designation debate.

• Saucedo: officers "transferred to fortify World Cup hosts"
• Militia arms: "smuggled from the U.S., grenades and drones"

WAPO: Mexico's president vows 'legal measures' after immigrant fatally shot by ICE
July 8, 2026 | 🔴

📰 ICE shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52 — a father of three, 30 years in Houston, driving to work. Sheinbaum: "we're preparing legal measures, obviously more significant ones." 🇲🇽

ICE's account — that he "weaponized his vehicle" — ran first; the family says he panicked and mistook masked, unmarked officers for intruders.

• ICE: he "weaponized his vehicle" to "run over" an officer
• Sheinbaum: "we cannot allow the mistreatment of our brothers and sisters"

🇲🇽📉 <u>MEXICAN INFLATION COOLS TO 3.55% — THE DOOM FORECASTS HAVE A DATA PROBLEM</u>

The gloom forecasts have a data problem. Mexican inflation fell to 3.55% in June — down from 4.45% in April — closing in on Banxico's 3% target, driven by cooling food and energy prices (jitomate and electricity leading the drop). Same week the IMF trimmed its Mexico growth call to 1.2%, the actual price data kept easing.

🇲🇽📊 <u>68% APPROVAL: THE 'CRISIS' NARRATIVE KEEPS LOSING TO THE DATA</u>

Seven of every ten Mexicans approve of President Sheinbaum — 68% in the latest poll. Almost two years in, after every prophecy of collapse over judicial reform, cartel operations and open US pressure, the mandate hasn't cracked. The people who live here keep answering the question the foreign press keeps getting wrong.
